doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

chapter: Rutgers and the Institute of Jazz Studies
title: LPs versus CDs, downloading, liner notes and Dan Morgenstern
summary: A patron insisted on the LP; Pelote dislikes downloading, and both credit liner notes and Morgenstern for their jazz education.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Yes. People do come in and use it. And I was shocked one day when somebody came in, just one of the community people in the Newark community – because we’re open to everybody, we’re not just open to students, it’s open to everybody – he came in and he wanted to hear a Miles Davis recording. But he said, “I don’t want to hear the CD, I want to hear the LP.” And so I did a double take and said, “You sure? I mean it’s the same record.” “No, no, no” he said, “I want to hear the LP. The LP sounds different.” So I got him the LP and he was happy as a clam. But that’s so rare, really, that somebody is that insistent on listening to an LP. A lot of times we give people LPs because there are no CD equivalents. And that’s still, unfortunately, the truth. And I hate to hear about the impending death of the CD because not everything has been switched over. There are still LPs that you’ll never see on CDs. And that’s a shame, if CDs are going to die.
Oh right. They’re not going to make them anymore.
And downloading? I’m sorry. Maybe it’s just what pains me is the old fogy that I am, I do not like downloading. I just don’t. I don’t.
I don’t care for it at all.
And I got a good deal of my jazz education from reading liner notes.
You know you’re in the record store and you’re reading and you learn who writes, who do you agree with, so I’m going to buy this because this person says this thing about it.

Yep. One of the first things I told Dan Morgenstern when I knew he was the Institute of Jazz Studies Director was, you know how many records I’ve bought strictly on the fact that you said it was a great record? And he gets all sheepish and everything.
Yeah, I was just going to say, “Well I hope you liked them.”
I said, “Dan, you’re the man.” You know.
